clue.text: Pay fine, also needing to return coppers

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the word for also is read from right to left

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
too means as well
the Bill is British slang for the police

explanation.surface: Someone must pay a penalty and also turn back towards the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bill is everyday British slang for the police force; 'fine' looks like a penalty to pay but is just the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot the bill is an idiom meaning to cover the cost of something, so it means to pay.

clue.text: Arab turning up very shortly

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the phrase reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: in a mo means in a moment, very soon

explanation.surface: An Arab will arrive any moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula, so its citizens are Arabs.

clue.text: Betrays family pair involved in famous archery feat?

definitions.text: family pair involved in famous archery feat?

blocks.note: first meaning: informs on someone

blocks.clueFragment: family pair involved in famous archery feat?
blocks.note: second meaning: William Tell and his boy, from whose head he shot an apple

explanation.surface: A father and son betray each other over a legendary archery stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Respace the answer as TELL SON: the Swiss hero William Tell and the son on whose head the apple sat.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell on someone is an idiom for reporting their wrongdoing, which betrays them.

clue.text: Socialise in mostly sweet hotel to the north

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the last letter is dropped
in a down clue heading north means the letters run upwards

blocks.note: a bonbon is a sweet
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mixing with people in a hotel's chocolate-box lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: BONBON loses its last N, H is added, and the whole runs upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, especially with people of higher status.

clue.text: Battered starter of bass fully consumed

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of bass
eaten up means wholly devoured

explanation.surface: A battered fish starter, wolfed down completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' and 'bass' set up a fish supper; battered means assaulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beaten up has been attacked and given a pounding, which is what battered means.

clue.text: Way to eat dip — item served in trattoria?

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a lane is a way or road
to sag is to dip

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to eat a dip at an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits the clue: 'Way to eat dip' is all wordplay, and the question mark admits the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a classic Italian baked pasta dish, likely on the menu of an Italian eatery.

clue.text: Goal that lady ignores? Flipping hell!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: the net is the goal in football
her refers to that lady
taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A goal she ignores, followed by a mild British curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping hell!' reads as one exclamation, but flipping is the anagram signal and hell the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The nether regions are the underworld, the place of damnation below the earth.

clue.text: Borderline impudence I heard at intervals

indicators.note: at intervals means every other one, so alternate letters are kept

blocks.note: front means cheek or brazenness
first, third and fifth letters of I heard

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they heard some borderline cheek now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borderline' reads as an adjective meaning dubious; here it is a noun, the line at a border.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the boundary line between two countries.

clue.text: Holds section of newspaper for capital feature

blocks.note: nelsons are wrestling holds
a column is a regular section of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper keeps space for a feature article in its capital edition.
explanation.walkthrough: A nelson is a wrestling hold with the arm under the opponent's armpit. 'Feature' reads as a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson's Column is the monument in Trafalgar Square, a landmark of London, Britain's capital city.

clue.text: English newspaper’s online reading material

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
the Daily Mail is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A British newspaper's website is offered as something to read on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is just 's = is, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages that arrive in your electronic inbox are text you read on a screen over the internet.

clue.text: Bar’s pair of cups one put back?

indicators.note: putting something back means returning it to a later spot, so the single letter is taken out and slotted in further along

blocks.note: a brassiere is a bra, a garment with two cups
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about why a bar's bra should be put back on.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of BRASSIERE and put it back two places later: BRASSERIE. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal restaurant serving drinks and simple food, a kind of bar.

clue.text: Son with the awful drinking trouble gets drop of the hard stuff

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so these letters are knocked out of shape
drinking means taking something in, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: S-O-N and T-H-E taken together as letters to rearrange
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A son with a drinking problem finally has a drop of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop of the hard stuff' looks like a shot of whisky; it is a falling lump of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A hailstone is a pellet of ice that falls from the sky, a solid drop of frozen rain.

clue.text: Clever clogs cutting single class

indicators.note: cutting here means removing, so the single letter is cut out of the longer word

blocks.note: a clever clogs is a very bright person, a genius
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A know-it-all skipping a lone class.
explanation.walkthrough: Clever clogs is British for a show-off brainbox; drop the I from GENIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a taxonomic rank grouping related species, so it is a category or kind.

clue.text: Record musical covers to express sorrow

indicators.note: to cover is to wrap round, so one word sits outside the other

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Rent is a Broadway rock musical

explanation.surface: A recording of a stage show is used to voice regret.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is Jonathan Larson's 1990s Broadway rock musical.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel and show remorse for wrongdoing, which is voicing regret.

clue.text: Go with platforms on, making feet feel better?

definitions.note: a phrase for an activity; the answer is the noun naming it

blocks.note: podia is the plural of podium, a platform
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Try wearing platform shoes to make your feet feel better.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'with platforms on' means the platforms sit on top. 'Platforms' suggests shoes, not stages.
explanation.definitionFit: Podiatry is the medical care and treatment of foot ailments, so it aims to help sore feet.

clue.text: Middle Easterner once in Suriname, travelling

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of the country's name move into a new order

blocks.note: the South American country's name used as letters

explanation.surface: An ancient Middle Eastern person is found travelling in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumer was an ancient civilisation in Mesopotamia, modern Iraq, so its people lived in that region long ago.

clue.text: In France, I admire cooked grouse

indicators.note: cooked means altered or prepared, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: je is French for I
taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A French diner admiring a cooked game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' and 'cooked' suggest the bird; grouse means a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeremiad is a long, mournful complaint, so it is a grumble or moan.

clue.text: Partridge, say, in dens, excited in mating periods

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order
in places the bird word inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as letters to rearrange
a partridge is a game bird; say marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Partridges getting excited in their dens during the breeding season.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about birds breeding, but mating here is the chess sense: delivering checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Endgames are the final phases of chess games, when checkmate is usually delivered.

clue.text: Way of playing ball cheers up a rotter at first

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word for cheers is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
git is British slang for a contemptible person
ta is British for thanks
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A sporting move in which the crowd cheers a villain at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' moves A GIT to the front, ahead of the ball and reversed cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction meaning agitated, an instruction for how a piece should be played.

clue.text: Official backs king in charge — is it irony?

indicators.note: going backwards means the word for official is read from right to left

blocks.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
R is short for rex, Latin for king
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A referee supporting a king in power — is that ironic?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irony' looks like the literary term; it is the adjective from iron, like silky from silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferric is the chemistry adjective for compounds containing iron, so it describes something iron-like.

clue.text: Horse is less jerky over time

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: evener means smoother, less jerky
T is short for time

explanation.surface: A horse moves less jerkily with time.
explanation.walkthrough: EVENER goes over T: EVEN(T)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for eventing, the equestrian sport combining dressage, cross-country and jumping.

clue.text: Execute career plan for ambitious teacher

blocks.note: first meaning: kill by cutting off the head
second meaning: split in two, the goal of becoming the headteacher

explanation.surface: Carrying out a career plan for a teacher who wants promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execute' looks like carry out a plan. A head is a British school principal.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead someone is to kill them by decapitation, a form of capital punishment.

clue.text: Muslim maybe in Quebec caught in fresh air current

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of air are put into a new arrangement
being caught in something means being trapped inside it

blocks.note: taken as letters to rearrange
I is the symbol for electric current
Quebec is Q in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Muslim in Quebec is caught in a fresh breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: IRA then I, with Q slipped between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Most people from Iraq follow Islam, so an Iraqi is an example of a Muslim, hence the hedge.

clue.text: The Spanish cheese left by Mike is very basic

indicators.note: left by means abandoned by, so that letter departs from the cheese

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
Emmental is a Swiss cheese
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Spanish cheese abandoned by someone called Mike is pretty basic.
explanation.walkthrough: EMMENTAL loses one of its Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental, relating to the simplest building blocks of something.

clue.text: Extremely tough words in puzzle

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of tough
words, as in having words, means an argument or row

explanation.surface: Very difficult vocabulary in a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for tough; it selects that word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to confuse or disconcert them, which is to puzzle them.

clue.text: Local banks are almost right for account

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
banks line both sides of a river, so one word flanks the others

blocks.note: a native is a local person
taken as written before trimming
R is short for right

explanation.surface: Local banks are nearly right in their accounting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like money; it is the sides of a river, holding the inserted letters just after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is a story or report of events, just as an account is a telling of what happened.

clue.text: Droning noise made by personnel in corporation

indicators.note: in places the staff word inside the body word

blocks.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum
HR is human resources, the personnel department

explanation.surface: A dull hum produced by the staff of a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company; it is jocular old British slang for a large stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a continuous low rhythmic humming sound, like that of an engine.

clue.text: Crook boasts about detective’s case, maybe a murder

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept
about means surrounding, so two words go round the selected letters

blocks.note: a hood is a hoodlum, a criminal
the first and last letters of detective
to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: A criminal brags about a detective's murder case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murder' looks like the crime; it is the collective noun for a flock of crows.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of crows is called a murder, so several of these grey-and-black birds could form one.
